item.title: Halloween Decorating Tips That Protect Your Security Deposit
item.description: Decorating your Redding rental for Halloween or the holidays? Use these damage-free hanging, lighting, and yard tips to protect your security deposit.
item.content:encoded:
Putting up Halloween and holiday decorations is part of making a house feel like home, and a few simple habits will keep your rental looking festive without risking damage or security deposit deductions later

Festive Porch, Full Deposit: How to Decorate Your Rental Without Leaving a Mark.


Driving through neighborhoods in Redding, Anderson, Shasta Lake, and Cottonwood in late October is one of the best parts of fall. Porch pumpkins, string lights, and creative yard displays make a street feel welcoming and lived in.


We love seeing residents enjoy the season and make the house they rent feel like home. Unlike an HOA with a thick binder of seasonal mandates, we do not hand out a list of special lease rules for Halloween or Christmas decorations. Instead, we always encourage good neighbor etiquette and smart, damage-free decorating habits so you can enjoy the holidays now without running into repair charges against your security deposit when you eventually move out.


Under California law, as summarized on the California Attorney General's landlord-tenant resource page , a security deposit cannot be used for ordinary wear and tear, but it can be used to repair damage beyond normal wear and tear caused by a resident or their guests. The good news is that almost every common holiday decorating mishap is easy to avoid with a few simple swaps.

 

1. Hang Indoor Cobwebs, Wreaths, and Lights Without Peeling the Paint

Interior drywall and painted trim are the number one place where holiday decorations leave an expensive footprint. Heavy-duty mounting tape, cheap novelty window clings, and thumbtacks can pull paint right down to the drywall paper or leave stained residue when the weather warms up.

Here is how to keep walls, doors, and windows clean:


  • Use removable damage-free hooks and pull the tab slowly. When taking down removable adhesive strips, always pull the tab straight down along the wall rather than yanking it toward you, which tears the paint.
  • Use over-the-door wreath hangers with a felt backing. Metal hooks work great on front and interior doors as long as they have a soft felt strip on the back so they do not scrape the top edge of the door paint every time it opens.
  • Skip duct tape, packaging tape, and hot glue on painted surfaces. Even a few days of sun on a window frame can bake standard tape adhesive onto vinyl or painted wood.
  • Test window clings on a small corner first. Some brightly colored gel clings can stain porous sills or painted wood trim if moisture condenses on the glass overnight.

 

2. Protect Roof Shingles, Fascia Boards, and Stucco Outside

When stringing orange lights for Halloween or transitioning into holiday lights next month, the biggest risk to the exterior of a home comes from staple guns, nails, and screws driven into the roof edge or siding. Puncturing roof shingles or flashing creates tiny entry points for water just as Redding's November and December rainstorms arrive. Nails and staples driven into wood fascia or stucco also leave chipped holes that require patching and painting later.


  • Use plastic gutter clips or shingle tabs instead of staples or nails. Plastic light clips slide onto rain gutters or under the front edge of a shingle without piercing anything, and they pop right off in January.
  • Never walk on tile or wet composition roofs. Beyond the personal safety risk, walking on roof tiles can crack them and lead to winter roof leaks.
  • Wrap porch railings and columns with zip ties or soft twine. Zip ties hold garlands, skeletons, and light strands securely in the wind without scratching the paint.

 

3. Watch for Sprinklers, Underground Lines, and Lawn Health in the Yard

Inflatables, tombstones, and yard stakes are fun for trick-or-treaters, but they can be hard on grass and irrigation systems if they stay in one spot too long.


  • Keep yard stakes shallow and away from sprinkler heads. Before pushing plastic or metal stakes into the lawn, check where the sprinkler heads and drip lines run so you do not puncture a PVC pipe or poly tubing underground.
  • Put inflatables on a timer and move heavy props occasionally. A large inflatable lying flat on damp grass all day blocks sunlight and traps moisture, which can leave a yellow dead patch in the lawn within a week.
  • Set carved pumpkins on a tray or porch mat. Real jack-o'-lanterns soften quickly in warm Northern California afternoons. Setting them on a plate or mat prevents rotting pumpkin juice from staining concrete steps or wood decking, and prevents mold from drawing pests to the front door.

 

4. Keep Walkways, Electrical Cords, and Porch Lights Safe for Visitors

Good holiday etiquette also means thinking about the neighbors, delivery drivers, and kids walking up your driveway after dark. According to the National Fire Protection Association's Halloween Fire Safety Tips , dried fall props like cornstalks, crepe paper, and fabric ghosts catch fire quickly when placed too close to heat sources.


  • Swap real candle flames for battery-operated LED tea lights. Battery candles inside jack-o'-lanterns and porch luminaries flicker just like the real thing without the fire risk around long costumes or dry leaves.
  • Use outdoor-rated extension cords and GFCI outlets. Never run indoor extension cords out through a pinched window screen or across a wet walkway where someone can trip.
  • Keep steps, handrails, and house numbers clear. Make sure trick-or-treaters and guests have a wide, well-lit path to the front door with no fake spiderwebs or cords stretched across face or ankle height.
  • Check your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Before plugging in seasonal lights and turning on the heater for the season, take thirty seconds to test your alarms. You can read more in our rental fire safety and smoke detector guide .

 

5. Be a Thoughtful Neighbor When the Night Winds Down

Part of living in a great neighborhood is looking out for the people next door. If your display includes motion-activated sound effects, strobe lights, or blower motors on yard inflatables, setting them on an evening timer so they turn off at a reasonable hour keeps the peace with neighbors who have sleeping kids, pets, or early work shifts. And once the holiday wraps up, taking decorations down in a timely manner keeps the neighborhood looking sharp and prevents fall winds and rain from tearing props loose or blowing them down the street.

��If you notice an exterior outlet that is not working properly, a loose porch railing, or a dark walkway light while setting up, let our team know through the online maintenance request portal so we can get it taken care of before guests arrive.

 

Wrap Up

You do not need a complicated rulebook to enjoy Halloween and the upcoming holiday season in a rental home. A little common sense, damage-free clips instead of nails and tape, battery candles instead of open flames, and consideration for your neighbors can help you enjoy the season while protecting your security deposit.

item.title: October 2026 Redding Rental Market Update for Property Owners
item.description: Before selling a Redding rental, owners should weigh taxes, depreciation, capital gains, 1031 options, and tenant risks to make a thoughtful hold-or-sell decision.
item.content:encoded:
Rates jump, accidental landlords arrive, and Redding rentals head into the rainy season. Here is what it means for your rental.

Introduction

October in Redding means cooler mornings, the first real rain on the way, and pumpkin patches popping up around town. It is also a month when the rental and sales markets start telling two different stories.


This month we cover our September numbers, a new kind of owner we are meeting more often, a jump in mortgage rates , a stove and refrigerator rule that is now in full swing, a quick winter-prep list, and a few ways we gave back in September.


��️ Redding Rental Market Update

Our portfolio vacancy is holding steady at about 6% as of October 11.

September was a busy month for our team:

  • 28 move-ins
  • 16 move-outs
  • 60 lease renewals

Sixty renewals tell us a lot of good residents are choosing to stay, and that is the best outcome for any owner. Every renewal is a month with no turnover costs and no empty home.


��Vacancies are ticking up a little, and we think we know why. More homes are entering the rental market , which brings us to this month's big topic.


�� Owner Insight: The Rise of the Accidental Landlord

We are meeting a lot of new owners right now. Many had a home for sale for a couple of months and could not get it sold. Now they want to rent it instead, and many are likely paying two mortgages while they wait. Many of them are also not willing to give up a great mortgage rate somewhere between 2% and 4%. We understand that. A rate like that is hard to walk away from. That extra inventory is a big reason vacancies are creeping up slightly in Redding.


So what is an accidental landlord ? It is someone who ends up renting out a home because of their situation, not because they set out to invest. Common reasons:

  • Moving for a new job
  • Buying a new home, planning to sell the old one, and then not being able to
  • Moving to a bigger city for better medical care during a life event


Most plan to rent for a few years. In our experience, most accidental landlords end up staying long-term landlords. They like the steady income, and they enjoy the tax benefits, especially depreciation. If you are new to that idea, our post on Rental Property Depreciation: Tax Deductions Every Landlord Should Know is a good place to start. As always, talk with your CPA about your own situation.


Know someone with a home that will not sell? Or are you in that spot yourself? We are happy to help. Start with a free rental analysis to see what the home could likely rent for.


�� Shasta County Sales Market Snapshot

In his October 2026 update, Josh Barker reports 30-year fixed rates around 7.75%, with some buyers seeing close to 8%. That is nearly a full point higher than a month or so ago. A buyer who qualified for about $400,000 last month may now qualify for closer to $360,000.


  • 208 homes sold in September, down about 9.2% from 229 a year earlier
  • Year-to-date, 2,100 sales versus 1,954 in 2025, still up about 7.5%
  • Homes are selling around 95% of original list price
  • Absorption is about 4.1 months, a balanced market


What it means for you: When payments jump, more households keep renting, which supports rental demand. It also means more homes that do not sell may turn into rentals. Clean, well-priced homes that are shown fast are more likely to lease first.


⚖️ Legislative Lowdown: AB 628 Is Now in Full Swing

A quick reminder. Under California Assembly Bill 628 , a working stove and a working refrigerator are now part of the basics a California rental must have (Civil Code Section 1941.1). It applies to leases entered into, amended, or extended on or after January 1, 2026. With renewals rolling in all year, it now covers a big share of homes.


  • The stove and fridge need to be in good working order
  • A recalled appliance does not count and needs to be repaired or replaced within 30 days of notice
  • A tenant can supply their own fridge, but only with specific written lease language


If a renewal is coming up on a home without appliances, let's plan for it now.


**This section is informational only and is not legal advice. Please review it with your attorney or trusted professional when needed.


��️ Seasonal Maintenance Tips

Redding can go from dry to drenched fast. A short fall checklist saves emergency calls later:


  • Service the heater and replace the filter before the first cold snap
  • Clear gutters and downspouts after the leaves drop
  • Look over the roof for loose or missing shingles
  • Wrap exposed pipes and hose bibs before freezing nights
  • Test smoke and CO alarms when daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1

 

�� Giving Back in September

September was a full month for our team in the community:

  • We sponsored and played in the Cronic Disaster Restoration Golf Fundraiser , with proceeds supporting Raising Shasta and the kids and families they serve across Shasta County.
  • We donated a raffle basket to Heroes on Paws , a benefit supporting local police K-9 units in Redding.


A big thank you to everyone who voted for us in the Best of the North State. Voting closed September 30, and we are truly grateful for every vote and kind word.


�� Fall Fun Around Redding

  • Redding Retro Halloween Night Market , Saturday, October 17, 6 to 9 PM, at 550 Cypress Ave
  • Downtown Fall Festival , Saturday, October 24, on Market Street, with a costume contest and downtown trick-or-treating from 3 to 6 PM
  • Hawes Haunts at Historic Hawes Farms, Friday and Saturday nights through October 31 (18+)


�� We're Always Here to Help

If you are prepping for winter, reviewing a renewal, or deciding between selling and renting, we are here to help.

At Authority Property Management , We Make Rentals Simple .

Website: www.authoritypm.com
